justification: detect_former_council gates which LGAs get DCP setbacks/site-coverage in the brief. A hand-maintained EPI->slug allow-list had gone stale: 14 onboarded LGAs (Canada Bay, Bayside, Burwood, Camden, Cumberland, Fairfield, Georges River, Parramatta, Randwick, Ryde, Strathfield, Sutherland Shire, The Hills, City of Sydney) had complete current rows in dcp_setback_controls but no map entry, so the function returned None and the brief silently served NO DCP setbacks for them. Found live on 17 Corden Ave, Five Dock (Canada Bay). This is a data-completeness defect affecting ~14/29 onboarded LGAs (>2% rule => Priority 1).

pre_impl.existing_data: dcp_setback_controls holds per-LGA setback/site-coverage rows keyed by an lga slug. Verified read-only 2026-06-19: 29 distinct lga slugs, 28 address-resolvable (nsw_statewide is a fallback). All 14 previously-unmapped LGAs have is_current rows with needs_review=0 and control/dev-type coverage at parity with the LGAs already mapped (canada_bay 40 rows, parramatta 51, georges_river 41).
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: ZONE_EPI_TO_LGA_SLUG was assumed to be the onboarding source of truth, but it was a stale hand-maintained list of 11 EPI strings; the data table had moved ahead of it. The Parramatta/Cumberland 'rows not yet complete' comment was demonstrably outdated (51 and 25 current rows, 0 needs_review).
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: No new data and no schema change. detect_former_council now, on a map miss, derives the slug from the EPI name (_slug_from_epi) and accepts it only if it is in DCP_ONBOARDED_SLUGS (a verified completeness gate). The explicit map is kept for special cases (Inner West suburb disambiguation, City of Sydney). Signature unchanged, so all 6 callers are unaffected.
pre_impl.external_source_error: The EPI name comes from the NSW Planning Portal (zone_epi). If the portal returns an unexpected instrument name, _slug_from_epi either returns None (no instrument phrase) or a slug that is not in DCP_ONBOARDED_SLUGS -> detect_former_council returns None, i.e. the pre-fix behaviour (no DCP setbacks). It can never resolve to the wrong LGA's data because the derived slug is validated against the onboarded set and then cross-checked against the parcel's PostGIS LGA boundary by _validate_former_council_postgis.
pre_impl.frontend_type: N/A - backend only. The brief's dcp_former_council stays Optional[str]; it is now populated for more LGAs but its type and the downstream DCPControls schema are unchanged. Capacity card remains unexposed (#513).
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: Before: a Canada Bay (and 13 other LGAs) brief showed 'former council could not be determined' and no setbacks/site-coverage - silent under-service of onboarded data. After: those LGAs resolve and their real DCP controls appear. The fix can only ADD correct DCP data or leave it absent (fail-safe); it cannot serve another LGA's setbacks.

functions.name: _slug_from_epi
functions.input: zone_epi string from the planning portal, e.g. 'Canada Bay Local Environmental Plan 2013'
functions.output: slugified council name ('canada_bay'), or None if no 'LOCAL ENVIRONMENTAL PLAN'/'LEP' phrase is present
functions.if_none: no instrument phrase -> returns None so a bare string cannot resolve to an LGA

functions.name: detect_former_council
functions.input: address and zone_epi (EPI name) from the portal
functions.output: an onboarded LGA slug for dcp_setback_controls, or None when the LGA is not onboarded
functions.if_none: map miss AND derived slug not in DCP_ONBOARDED_SLUGS -> None (caller serves no DCP setbacks, same as before the fix)

values: N/A - no regulatory values are hardcoded. DCP_ONBOARDED_SLUGS is a curated list of LGA identifiers (not planning values); each was verified to have complete current rows in dcp_setback_controls on 2026-06-19. The actual setback numbers are fetched from the DB at request time, unchanged by this PR.
queries: N/A - this function performs no database queries; it returns a slug that downstream code (fetch_dcp_setbacks) uses in its existing WHERE lga = %s AND is_current query.

break_it.scenario: A Canada Bay address whose EPI is 'Canada Bay Local Environmental Plan 2013' (the live 17 Corden Ave case)
break_it.what_happens: Old map had no Canada Bay entry, so detect_former_council returned None and the brief served no DCP setbacks or site-coverage despite 40 current rows existing
break_it.repro: detect_former_council('17 Corden Ave, Five Dock NSW 2046', 'Canada Bay Local Environmental Plan 2013')
break_it.how: _slug_from_epi derives 'canada_bay', which is in DCP_ONBOARDED_SLUGS; test_canada_bay_real_string_is_the_17_corden_case asserts it returns 'canada_bay'

break_it.scenario: An LGA that has a valid LEP name but no complete DCP data in the table (e.g. Wollongong)
break_it.what_happens: Naive slugify-and-trust would enable an LGA whose setbacks are not extracted, leaking empty or partial controls into the brief
break_it.repro: detect_former_council('1 Crown St, Wollongong NSW', 'Wollongong Local Environmental Plan 2009')
break_it.how: the derived 'wollongong' is not in DCP_ONBOARDED_SLUGS so the function returns None; test_unonboarded_lga_still_returns_none pins this completeness gate

break_it.scenario: The City of Sydney whose instrument is 'Sydney LEP' so the slug differs from the DCP slug
break_it.what_happens: Generic derivation yields 'sydney' which does not equal the DCP slug 'city_of_sydney', so Sydney would silently get no setbacks
break_it.repro: detect_former_council('1 George St, Sydney NSW', 'Sydney Local Environmental Plan 2012')
break_it.how: an explicit ZONE_EPI_TO_LGA_SLUG entry maps 'SYDNEY LOCAL ENVIRONMENTAL PLAN' -> 'city_of_sydney'; test_city_of_sydney_special_case_maps_via_explicit_entry asserts it

break_it.scenario: A non-EPI string with no instrument phrase is passed as zone_epi
break_it.what_happens: A bare council name like 'Canada Bay' could slugify to 'canada_bay' and falsely resolve an LGA without a real LEP context
break_it.how: _slug_from_epi requires a 'LOCAL ENVIRONMENTAL PLAN'/'LEP' phrase and returns None otherwise; test_non_lep_string_does_not_resolve covers '', 'Canada Bay'

break_it.scenario: An Inner West boundary suburb that must still disambiguate to its former council
break_it.what_happens: Refactoring the resolution order could break the Inner West suburb to former-council path and mis-route Haberfield and similar suburbs
break_it.repro: detect_former_council('12 Dalhousie St, Haberfield NSW 2045', 'Inner West Local Environmental Plan 2022')
break_it.how: the explicit map still matches Inner West first and the suburb disambiguation block is unchanged; test_inner_west_still_disambiguates_by_suburb asserts 'ashfield'

break_it.scenario: The portal returns the abbreviated 'LEP' form rather than the full instrument phrase
break_it.what_happens: If only the full 'LOCAL ENVIRONMENTAL PLAN' phrase were handled, abbreviated names would fail to resolve and lose DCP data
break_it.how: _slug_from_epi also cuts on ' LEP'; test_lep_abbreviation_form_also_resolves asserts 'sutherland_shire'

post_merge.manual_verify: Re-run a brief for an address in each newly-resolved LGA (start with 17 Corden Ave, Five Dock = Canada Bay) and confirm DCP setbacks/site-coverage now appear and the 'former council could not be determined' advisory is gone. When onboarding a future LGA's DCP data, add its slug to DCP_ONBOARDED_SLUGS (and an explicit ZONE_EPI_TO_LGA_SLUG entry only if its instrument name does not slugify to its DCP slug).
